Il nemico numero uno è il caldo. Un term: Enemy number one is heat. A radiator, a stove or sun through the window can warp a record in a single afternoon. Keep your records in a lived-in room, where the temperature stays stable, away from heat sources.
Anche l'umidità fa danni: le copertine s: Humidity does damage too: sleeves stain and buckle, and mould can appear. Damp cellars and lofts that turn into ovens in summer are the worst places for a collection.
Le buste interne di carta originali prot: The original paper inner sleeves protect the record, but over time they can scuff the surface and leave residue. Anti-static inner sleeves cost little and keep the record cleaner. A clear outer sleeve protects the cover from dust and wear, especially on records you play often.
Prendi il disco per il bordo e per l'eti: Hold the record by the edge and the centre label, without touching the grooves: fingers leave grease that traps dust. Put it back in its sleeve right after playing, and do not leave it on the turntable or lying around unprotected.
Prima di ogni ascolto basta una passata: Before each play a pass with a carbon-fibre brush is enough. For second-hand or very dirty records there are cleaning fluids and record-cleaning machines made for the job.
Una collezione ordinata si ascolta di pi: An organised collection gets played more. Many people sort records by genre and then by artist; others keep the records of the moment next to the turntable. In open record storage the spines and sleeves stay in view, and choosing what to play becomes part of the pleasure.

Why a turntable is so sensitive.
La puntina legge movimenti di pochi mill: The stylus reads movements of a few thousandths of a millimetre cut into the groove. It cannot tell the groove from everything else: if the cabinet vibrates, if the floor moves under footsteps, if the bass from the speakers makes the top shake, the stylus reads that too and sends it to the amplifier.
Il risultato può essere un rimbombo nei: The result can be boomy bass, a muddled sound, the stylus skipping when someone walks by. In the worst cases you get feedback: the sound from the speakers makes the turntable vibrate, the stylus picks it up, the amplifier sends it back to the speakers and the boom grows.
La prima difesa è il mobile. Deve essere: The first line of defence is the cabinet. It should be stable, not wobble when you touch it and not bend under the weight. A light cabinet or one with thin shelves acts like a sounding box; a solid wood cabinet, with thick, well-jointed shelves, damps vibrations instead of amplifying them.

Un pannello assorbente è fatto di un mat: An absorbing panel is made of a soft, porous material, such as rock wool or polyester fibre. It soaks up part of the sound's energy, so the reflection comes back weaker.
Un pannello che diffonde ha invece una s: A diffusing panel, on the other hand, has an irregular surface, with blocks or slats at different depths. It doesn't take energy out of the room: it sends it back in many directions and slightly staggered in time, instead of all at once towards you. The reflection is still there, but it arrives scattered and doesn't get in the way.
Un piedino disaccoppiante è fatto di un: A decoupling foot is made of an elastic material that deforms under the weight: when the shelf vibrates, the foot squashes and stretches and damps the vibrations before they reach the turntable. A rigid foot, on the other hand, passes them all through.
Una prova semplice: batti forte le mani: A simple test: clap your hands loudly in the middle of the room. If you hear a metallic echo ringing between two parallel walls, those walls need a panel. Repeat the test once it's up.
